senses.definition: A procedural plan, usually but not necessarily tabular in nature, indicating a sequence of operations and the planned times at which those operations are to occur.
examples: To complete on time, we must follow the schedule.

senses.definition: A serial record of items, systematically arranged.
(law) A written or printed table of information, often forming an annex or appendix to a statute or other regulatory instrument, or to a legal contract.

subsenses.definition: (US, law, often capitalized) One of the five divisions into which controlled substances are classified, or the restrictions denoted by such classification.
examples: Heroin is a Schedule I drug with a high potential for abuse.

quotes.text: Currently, cannabis/marijuana is classified as a Schedule I drug, meaning it defined as having “no currently accepted medical use and a high potential for abuse.” This is the same designation given to LSD, heroin and ecstasy.
quotes.reference: 2022 October 13, Shawn Radcliffe, “What Happens if Marijuana is No Longer Classified as Schedule 1 Drug?”, in healthline, archived from the original on 21 Apr 2023:

subsenses.definition: (Australia, law, medicine) One of the nine schedules of the Standard for the Uniform Scheduling of Medicines and Poisons. Identical to the American usage above.

senses.definition: (computer science) An allocation or ordering of a set of tasks on one or several resources.
(obsolete) A slip of paper; a short note.

quotes.text: He demands the blood-written schedule back from the demon, who refuses to give it up
quotes.reference: 1900, John the Stylite, translated by Agnes Smith Lewis, Select Narratives of Holy Women (Studia Sinaitica; X), Logos edition, London; Cambridge University Press Warehouse: C. J. Clay and Sons, page xxix:

senses.definition: (transitive) To plan (an activity or event) for a specific date or time.
examples: The next elections are scheduled on the twentieth of November.

senses.definition: (transitive) To add (a name) to the list of those participating in an event; to reserve a place or time for.
examples: I am scheduled for classes next month.
I'll schedule you for three-o'clock then.

senses.definition: (transitive, Australia, medicine) To admit (a person) to hospital as an involuntary patient under a schedule of the applicable mental health law.
examples: whether or not to schedule a patient

senses.definition: (transitive, US) To classify as a controlled substance.

quotes.text: Many harm reduction groups and drug policy experts question the long-term efficacy of scheduling xylazine.
